answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to microfluidic viscometry. A node authenticates by applying an acoustic pulse to a shear-mode quartz resonator immersed in a nectar droplet, recording the damping curve. An attacker must operate discrete sampling hardware and fluidic cells per identity, incurring substantial capital and maintenance costs. However, ambient temperature shifts alter liquid viscosity, requiring periodic recalibration to avoid false rejections.
